question: Should ClawHub allow post-publish changelog edits, and what authorization/audit model should guard that metadata?
rationale: This changes public release metadata after publication, so code inspection cannot decide the product/security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Audited owner/admin edit path
options.body: Allow publisher-authorized edits for skill and package version changelogs, update latest summaries atomically, and write visible audit history for the change.

options.title: Immutable changelogs
options.body: Keep release changelogs immutable and document that corrections require publishing a replacement version or staff moderation action.

options.title: Staff-only correction path
options.body: Permit only moderators/admins to correct changelogs through an operational tool for abuse, legal, or trust-and-safety cases.

recommendation.title: Audited owner/admin edit path
recommendation.body: Allow publisher-authorized edits for skill and package version changelogs, update latest summaries atomically, and write visible audit history for the change.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties Patrick-Erichsen most strongly to the current CLI, backend publish, package release, and version-history surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
